questions.question: If your car breaks down on a highway, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in your car and wait for help.
Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
Honk your horn at passing cars.
Flash your headlights at oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: Turn on your hazard flashers and carefully exit the road. Park as far off the road as possible so other drivers can see you. Lift your hood to show your car is disabled.

questions.question: You can reduce the risk of hydroplaning by:

options.text: Driving through shallow water.
Driving faster.
Driving slower.
Driving through deep water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving slower.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast in wet conditions. Slow down to reduce the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: Before turning left, you must:

options.text: Honk your horn.
Let oncoming vehicles pass first.
Move to the right side of your lane.
Wait for oncoming traffic to get a red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let oncoming vehicles pass first.
questions.explanation: When turning left at a traffic light, you must let pedestrians and oncoming traffic go first.

questions.question: Round signs warn drivers about:

options.text: No passing zones.
School zones.
Railroad crossings ahead.
Hospitals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossings ahead.
questions.explanation: Round signs warn drivers that a railroad crossing is coming. Drive with extra care when you see this sign.

questions.question: Children age ____ and younger should not sit in the front seat.
questions.explanation: Children age 12 and younger must sit in the back seat. They should be secured with a seat belt or child safety seat.

questions.question: Stress can affect your driving by:

options.text: Reducing your ability to focus on the road.
Decreasing your chances of an accident.
Making you fall asleep at the wheel.
Making you more aware of other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reducing your ability to focus on the road.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions like worry, anger, fear, or sadness hurt your driving ability. Stress reduces your concentration. If you feel emotionally upset, do not drive.

questions.question: ____ greatly increase stopping distance and crash severity.

options.text: High speeds
Low speeds
Driving at night
Driving uphill

questions.correctAnswerText: High speeds
questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the longer it takes to stop and the worse a crash will be. High speed greatly increases the force of impact.

questions.question: Is it legal to park in the access aisles next to handicap parking spaces?

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: You cannot park in handicap access aisles. These spaces are needed for wheelchairs and wheelchair lifts.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving on wet roads?

options.text: When you drive faster, your tires work less effectively.
Water does not affect cars with good tires.
Deep water is safer than shallow water.
When you slow down, the road becomes more slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you drive faster, your tires work less effectively.
questions.explanation: On wet roads, faster speeds make tires less effective at pushing water away. If you drive too fast, your tires lose grip and you will hydroplane, or slide on water.

questions.question: Why does night driving require extra caution?

options.text: Traffic moves faster at night.
There is more traffic at night.
Drivers cannot see as well in the dark.
More accidents happen at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers cannot see as well in the dark.
questions.explanation: It is darker at night, so drivers cannot see as well. You must use your headlights from 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise, or whenever people and vehicles are not visible for 500 feet ahead.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spot before changing lanes?

options.text: Look in the left side mirror.
Look in the right side mirror.
Look in the rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.
questions.explanation: To check your blind spot before changing lanes, look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.

questions.question: When must a driver yield to a pedestrian?

options.text: Always, even if the pedestrian is crossing carelessly.
Only when the pedestrian is in a crosswalk.
Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road as the driver.
Only if the pedestrian signals the driver to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always, even if the pedestrian is crossing carelessly.
questions.explanation: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians in the street, even if they are crossing against a red light or crossing carelessly.

questions.question: Increasing your speed is the best way to avoid losing control on wet roads.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: On wet roads, your tires can ride up on the water surface and cause you to lose control. This is called hydroplaning. The best way to avoid this is to slow down when driving on wet roads.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrians only.
Intersection ahead.
Hiking trails ahead.
School crossing ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: School crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a school crossing is ahead.

questions.question: What does an orange-colored sign mean?

options.text: The start of a no passing zone.
A railroad crossing is ahead.
A school zone is ahead.
Construction work is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Construction work is ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange signs with black symbols warn drivers about construction, maintenance, and emergency work.

questions.question: What is the correct way to use a freeway exit ramp?

options.text: Slow down before entering the exit ramp.
Slow down after you move onto the exit ramp.
Keep your speed the same on the exit ramp.
Pass slower traffic on the exit ramp.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down after you move onto the exit ramp.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down until you move onto the exit ramp. Then reduce your speed.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle with sirens and/or flashing lights approaches you, what must you do?

options.text: Pull to the right and stop.
Pull to the right and slow down.
Pull to the right and turn on your four-way flashers.
Stop and let the vehicle pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle uses lights and sirens, you must immediately drive to the right side of the road and stop.

questions.question: At night, you may use parking lights instead of headlights.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: You cannot drive at night using only parking lights. You must use your headlights when it is dark or when visibility is poor.

questions.question: It starts to rain while you are driving. What should you do?

options.text: Drive faster than other traffic.
Drive at the maximum posted speed limit.
Slow down.
Drive very close behind the vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: When rain reduces visibility, slow down and turn on your headlights. If rain is very heavy and you cannot see well, pull off the road and stop until it improves.

questions.question: What are the most effective safety restraints in a crash?

options.text: Only a lap and shoulder belt.
Only an airbag.
Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.
No safety restraints.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.
questions.explanation: Safety belts double your chance of surviving a crash. Airbags used with safety belts provide extra protection in front-end crashes. You should wear both shoulder and lap belts.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop completely. Look for pedestrians and traffic crossing.
Slow down without stopping completely.
Stop completely and wait for a green light.
Slow down and look for traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely. Look for pedestrians and traffic crossing.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign is always a stop sign. You must stop completely and look for pedestrians and crossing traffic. Wait until the intersection is clear before moving forward.

questions.question: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the road shoulder, you should:

options.text: Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the pavement.
Stop your car at the edge of the road.
Slow down and carefully turn back onto the pavement.
Keep your speed and turn sharply back onto the pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and carefully turn back onto the pavement.
questions.explanation: If your wheels drop off the pavement, reduce your speed gently without braking hard. Then carefully turn back onto the pavement. Watch for other traffic when you return to the road.

questions.question: While driving, your wheels slip off the edge of the road. You should:

options.text: Jerk the steering wheel to force the vehicle back onto the pavement.
Speed up and gradually steer back onto the pavement.
Slam on the brakes and stop.
Gently brake to slow down. Turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently brake to slow down. Turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement safely.
questions.explanation: If your wheels leave the road, keep them off the pavement and reduce speed by gently pressing the brakes. When your speed is safe, turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement. Do not sharply jerk the wheel to force your vehicle back.

questions.question: A driver making a left turn must yield to a bicyclist coming from the opposite direction.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming bicycles just as you would to oncoming cars. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn. Proceed only when the way is clear.

questions.question: You are waiting in a line at a stop sign. The vehicles ahead have passed through with no crossing traffic. You:

options.text: May proceed through without stopping again.
Must stop completely at the stop sign before proceeding.
May slowly roll past the stop sign.
May follow the vehicle ahead without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stop completely at the stop sign before proceeding.
questions.explanation: You must always stop completely at a stop sign and check for traffic before proceeding. Do not skip this step even if other vehicles have already passed through.
